title: Mice and Cheese
summary: Two mice must each eat exactly one type of cheese from n different types.
statement: Two mice must each eat exactly one type of cheese from n different types. The first mouse earns points from reward1[], while the second mouse earns from reward2[]. Given reward1, reward2, and a non-negative integer k, find the maximum points the first mouse can achieve by eating exactly k types of cheese.
constraints: Exactly one mouse eats each cheese type.
Mouse one must eat exactly k types; mouse two eats all remaining types.
Return the maximum total reward earned by both mice.
hints: Start by assigning every cheese to mouse two.
For cheese i, switching it to mouse one changes the total by reward1[i]-reward2[i].
Sort those gains and take exactly the largest k.
Every legal allocation is a size-k set of switches, and the k largest independent gains maximize their sum.
editorial: Every legal allocation is a size-k set of switches, and the k largest independent gains maximize their sum.

tests.explanation: Giving mouse one the last two cheeses and mouse two the first two earns fifteen.
Mouse one must take both cheeses, and the total reward is two.
